text: You're online, casually browsing a new gadget. You check its features, maybe add it to cart, then click away. You just wanted to explore options.
But now, everywhere you click – news sites, social media, other apps – ads for that exact gadget appear. It feels like the internet is following you.
You wonder, "Is my phone listening? Is it reading my mind?" It feels uncanny, like a digital stalker knows your thoughts.
It's "retargeting." A small, anonymous digital marker remembers your interest, not your identity. Advertisers use this to remind you.
This is efficient for businesses, but can feel repetitive or invasive. "Frequency capping" limits how often you see the same ad.
The ads will still pop up, but now you see the system. It's a predictable reminder, not a creepy mind-reader.
